blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — Preparing for crises beyond the battlefield, troops of the Army’s 10th Infantry Division underwent an intensive three-day medical training to boost their disaster response and frontline life-saving capabilities. The 10ID Station Hospital spearheaded the basic life support and standard first aid training at Camp General Manuel T. Yan Sr. in Mawab, Davao de Oro, from Oct. 29 to 31. In an emailed advisory on Monday, Maj. Ruben Gadut, 10ID spokesperson, said trainers from the Philippine Navy Nursing Service guided the soldiers to master cardiopulmonary resuscitation, automated external defibrillator operation, bleeding control, and wound management.
